title: Let package actions wait for the voice check

slides.title: The voice check expires before it can answer
slides.say: Before JARVIS can prepare a package action, a separate check must establish what you asked him to do. The approved design allows two seconds. The measured supported-model requests needed just over three seconds. JARVIS therefore refuses the action and leaves reading available. He has not sent a message or changed a package.

blocks.lead: A request to ask the sender produces no draft when the check expires.

points: Measured checks completed after the current limit.
No deadline or live model setting has been changed.

slides.title: A longer check still does not approve a message
slides.say: This decision changes how long JARVIS may wait to establish your request. A successful check can prepare a capture. You still hear or review the exact message and approve it for its recipient before it goes. If you permit the pause, we will retest with a supported configuration before release. This vote does not claim that trial has passed.

points: The configured model and the complete voice flow still need a runtime trial.

decisions.question: May package actions pause briefly so the voice check can finish?
decisions.say: I recommend allowing the short pause and retesting. The measured checks completed in about three seconds, while the current limit ends them at two. This authorizes a five-second maximum for this check, with no change to capture approval. Keeping the current limit leaves late checks unable to authorize package actions.

options.name: Allow a short pause and retest
options.says: Allow up to five seconds for this check. Retest before release. Sending still needs my separate approval.

options.name: Keep the current limit
options.says: Keep two seconds. Late checks refuse package actions. Hold release of voice package actions until a configuration meets that limit.

decisions.reason: The measured supported-model checks completed after the current limit, so waiting briefly lets us test the intended voice flow.
